sources: THURSDAY Oct 22 2026 EARLY RUN (06:15 UTC, before the US open). US cash closes are WEDNESDAY Oct 21; oil, metals and FX carry live Thursday European-session quotes. HEADLINE 1 - THE OIL SHOCK ESCALATED OVERNIGHT, FROM THREAT TO ATTACK. Houthi forces STRUCK a Saudi oil field and an international airport, and the United States ordered non-emergency personnel out of the kingdom. Brent is 111.1-111.2 USD/Bbl, plus about 2.1-2.2 pct on the day (OilPrice 111.10, TradingEconomics 111.11-111.19, WTI 98.98). This is the first run in which the Gulf risk premium reflects an actual strike on Saudi production infrastructure rather than threats, and it is the fourth consecutive run with Brent at or above 110. Iran talks remain stalled: Araqchi says Iran has no trust whatsoever in the US administration and the Iranian president says talks cannot proceed under the blockade, so the Hormuz reopening offer is now effectively off the table as a near-term relief valve. Note cappnotes has Brent December futures closing Wednesday at only 108.82 (plus 0.03 pct) with an intraday pop above 110, so this run captures a genuine Thursday-morning gap of roughly 2 dollars. Trend up and by a wide margin the most important tile on the board. HEADLINE 2 - THE POST-SELLOFF NFCI LANDED, AND IT LANDED BENIGN. This was flagged as the single most important pending number last run. FRED NFCI for week ending Oct 16 - the week that contains the Oct 16 rout - printed minus 0.496 versus minus 0.502 the week before (path minus 0.528, minus 0.518, minus 0.508, minus 0.502, minus 0.496). Financial conditions tightened by 0.006 of an index point, which is statistical noise. Conditions remain clearly looser than average and have drifted toward zero by only 0.03 over five weeks. The rout did NOT transmit into aggregate financial conditions. Trend flat. The next read is Oct 28. HEADLINE 3 - BUT CREDIT WIDENED AGAIN, AND THAT IS NOW THE DIVERGENCE. FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2 posted Oct 20 at 3.33 pct, up another 4bp from 3.29 Oct 19 (3.31 Oct 16, 3.23 Oct 15, 3.25 Oct 14). HY OAS is now 333bp, the widest print of the month, plus 10bp on the week and plus 21bp from the 312 top of the band that held through early October. Credit has not retraced the Oct 16 widening at all - it has extended it, on a day when equities rallied. This is the third consecutive run in which high yield spreads move the wrong way while every equity-side risk measure improves. EQUITY VOL - THIRD STRAIGHT FALL, SPIKE FULLY UNWOUND. VIX closed Oct 21 at 16.68, minus 3.64 pct, the third consecutive decline and the lowest since Oct 15. Path: 16.87 Oct 14, 16.46 Oct 15, 19.99 Oct 16, 18.44 Oct 19, 17.31 Oct 20, 16.68 Oct 21. VIX is now BELOW where it stood a week before the spike in Oct 14 terms and within 0.2 of the Oct 15 level, so the Oct 16 event is fully retraced in equity vol. Flat on the week. Stocks rallied: S and P 500 7,757.17 plus 0.58 pct, Nasdaq 26,702.86 plus 1.05 pct. RATES: FRED T10Y2Y Oct 20 0.33 (0.38 Oct 19, 0.35 Oct 16, 0.33 Oct 15, 0.37 Oct 14) - the curve FLATTENED 5bp on Tuesday, giving back the steepening of the prior session, and is exactly where it was a week ago, so flat. FRED has NOT posted Oct 21 - the FRED graph service was partly under maintenance this run and the T10Y2Y page still lists Oct 21 as the next release, so Oct 20 is the newest available spread. The 10Y closed Oct 21 at 5.13 pct, plus 1bp (2Y 4.79 pct on the Oct 20 Treasury par curve). FRED T5YIFR DID post Oct 21 at 2.34 pct (2.31 Oct 20, 2.32 Oct 19, 2.33 Oct 16, 2.31 Oct 15) - 5y5y breakevens ticked up 3bp to the TOP of the 2.31-2.34 band they have held for weeks. Still flat on the week and still the most reassuring number on the board, but with Brent gapping through 111 on a physical attack this is the tile to watch for the first crack: a decisive break above 2.35 would be the bond market finally conceding the oil shock is inflationary. LABOUR - CARRIED, RELEASE TODAY: FRED ICSA week ending Oct 10 199k, sixth straight week in a 198-199k range. The next print releases TODAY Oct 22 at 12:30 UTC, AFTER this run, so it lands tomorrow. Labour remains the strongest tile. REAL ECONOMY - ALL CARRIED: building permits 1,400k SAAR (September, released Oct 20); consumer sentiment 46.3 (UMich October preliminary, five-month low) trend down; ISM Manufacturing 54.5 (September, next Nov 2); LEI y/y minus 0.7 pct - the September LEI releases TODAY Oct 22 at 14:00 UTC, also after this run; Sahm Rule 0.00 (September, next Nov 6, trigger plus 0.50). DOLLAR AND GROWTH PROXY: DXY 101.59 (Oct 21 close 101.69 minus 0.04 pct, Thursday European session minus 0.10 pct) - down about 0.5 pct on the week and STILL refusing to bid on a FOURTH run of Brent above 110, now with an actual strike on Saudi infrastructure. A dollar that will not rally on a Gulf supply attack is the single strangest reading on this board and has been for a week. Trend down. Growth proxy 1.57 (copper 6.44 USD/Lbs minus 1.54 pct, gold 4,090.88 USD/t.oz minus 1.21 pct; 6.44/4090.88*1000 = 1.574). Both legs sold off together, so the ratio barely moved and is where it was a week ago - flat. Gold is now down five straight sessions from 4,181 and has broken below 4,100 despite the Gulf escalation, which is as odd as the dollar. MONETARY PLUMBING - STILL BLIND, SEVENTH RUN: the 3M SOFR-OIS spread was searched again and every free source serves only the SOFR level (3.87 pct) or an OIS rate, never the spread, so 0bp is CARRIED AS A STANDING ASSUMPTION, NOT A MEASUREMENT. The EUR/USD 3M cross-currency basis is also CARRIED AS AN ASSUMPTION at minus 10bp - no free source publishes it. Global liquidity 1 (stable) is a judgement call: no balance-sheet regime change found for the Fed, ECB, PBOC or BOJ this run. Two assumed tiles and one judgement tile out of eighteen, unchanged for a seventh run. MOVE 101.70 Oct 20 (101.30 Oct 19, 101.10 Oct 16, 102.49 Oct 15, 99.06 Oct 14) - no Oct 21 print on any free source. Rate vol is flat on the week and has hovered around 100 for over two weeks, remarkably well behaved through both the equity rout and the oil shock. FED: Oct 27-28 FOMC next week, fed funds target 3.75-4.00 pct, hold remains the heavy consensus. INFRASTRUCTURE: git healthy, working tree clean at start apart from the usual untracked junk, no ACTIVE HEAD.lock or index.lock, this scheduled session remains the sole writer of data.json (GitHub Action disabled since Oct 17), BDTI stayed removed. NOTE: .git now holds roughly 150 RENAMED lock files (HEAD.lock.dead.*, index.lock.stale.* and similar) accumulated because this session cannot delete files in the folder - they are harmless but should be cleared. STILL OPEN - SECURITY, SEVENTH RUN: the origin remote is an HTTPS URL with a GitHub personal access token in plain text in .git/config. Fine-grained and repo-scoped, but it should be rotated and replaced with an SSH remote. Also still present: untracked junk in the repo root - _stale_git_locks/, _wtest, __pycache__/ and outputs/. PICTURE: the board has split cleanly in two and the split got sharper. Everything FINANCIAL is healing: VIX has fully retraced the Oct 16 spike over three sessions, stocks made new highs, the post-rout NFCI came in essentially unchanged and still loose, rate vol is flat near 100, breakevens are inside their band, claims are below 200k for a sixth week. Everything PHYSICAL and CREDIT is deteriorating: Houthis have now actually struck Saudi oil infrastructure, the US is pulling diplomats, Iran talks are dead, Brent gapped through 111, and high yield spreads widened for a third consecutive run to 333bp - the widest of the month - on a day equities rallied 0.6 pct. The honest read is that the equity market has decided the Oct 16 wobble was noise and is trading accordingly, while the credit market and the oil market are both saying something is still wrong. When those two disagree this persistently, credit has historically been the one to believe. WATCH, IN ORDER OF WEIGHT: whether Brent holds above 111 or the strike premium fades, and whether any Saudi production is actually offline; whether HY OAS keeps widening past 333 or finally retraces toward 312; whether 5y5y breakevens break above 2.35, which would be the first inflation-expectations crack of this oil shock; claims and September LEI TODAY Oct 22; the Oct 27-28 FOMC; rotating the embedded PAT.
